title: Magnetic Fields
page_title: Magnetic Fields | Cambridge (CIE) IGCSE Physics Revision Notes 2021

blocks.name: Magnetic fields
blocks.definition:
- Describe a magnetic field as a region in which a magnetic pole experiences a force
- Draw the pattern and direction of magnetic field lines around a bar magnet
 - State that the direction of a magnetic field at a point is the direction of the force on the N pole of a magnet at that point

blocks.md: - A magnetic field is defined as:
**A region in which a magnetic pole experiences a force**

blocks.text: Magnetic field around a bar magnet

blocks.md:
- The magnetic field is **strongest at the poles**

  - Therefore, the magnetic field lines are **closer** together at the ends of the magnets
- The magnetic field becomes **weaker as the distance from the magnet increases**

  - Therefore, the magnetic field lines get **further apart**

blocks.alt: Lines leave the north pole of the magnet with arrows indicating the direction of the field and curve around to enter the south pole of the magnet. The lines are closer together near the magnet.
blocks.caption: Magnetic field lines are directed from the north pole of a magnet to the south pole

blocks.md:
- Field lines always have an **arrow** indicating the **direction** of the field line

  - The direction of the field line shows the **direction **in which the magnetic **force** would act
  - The field lines always go **from** a **north** pole **to** a **south** pole

blocks.name: Magnetic field strength
blocks.definition:
- Explain that magnetic forces are due to interactions between magnetic fields
 - Know that the relative strength of a magnetic field is represented by the spacing of the magnetic field lines

blocks.md:
- Magnetic forces are due to interactions between magnetic fields

  - Two bar magnets can [repel or attract](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/physics/cie/23/revision-notes/4-electricity-and-magnetism/4-1-simple-phenomena-of-magnetism/4-1-1-magnetism/?_ai=internal-linking)
- This is shown by the magnetic field lines between the two magnets:

blocks.alt: A diagram demonstrating magnetic fields between two pairs of bar magnets, where blue lines with arrows represent the magnetic field lines. Field lines flow directly from the north pole of the left magnet to the south pole of the right magnet for two attracting bar magnets, indicating a strong magnetic field. For two bar magnets with like poles, the blue field lines bend sharply away from each other without touching or crossing, demonstrating repulsion.
blocks.caption: Magnetic field lines for attracting and repelling bar magnets

blocks.md:
- The **strength** of the magnetic field is shown by the **spacing** of the magnetic field lines

  - If the magnetic field lines are **close together** then the magnetic field will be **strong**
  - If the magnetic field lines are **far apart** then the magnetic field will be **weak**

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
If you are asked to draw the magnetic field around a bar magnet remember to indicate both the **direction** of the magnetic field and the **strength** of the magnetic field. You can do this by:

- adding arrows pointing away from the north pole and towards the south pole
- making sure the magnetic field lines are further apart as the distance from the magnet increases
